description:
GOAL: Let an fz C extern receive bytes into a runtime-owned mutable binary and return the byte count, so libraries can call POSIX `read(2)` directly without a File-specific Rust bridge.

SIGNAL:
- an explicit C-ABI out-buffer contract passes writable runtime storage and a capacity to C
- the returned byte count produces a correctly sized immutable fz binary
- invalid/oversized counts fail loudly
- interp, JIT, and AOT agree
- File can use raw descriptors and bare `open`/`read`/`write`/`close` calls for path IO

STRATEGY: Design one generic output-buffer marshal class and ownership boundary; prove it with a minimal C fixture before migrating File from `FILE *` helpers.
title: Add owned binary output buffers for C externs
